title: Runtime Authorization Fabric: Policy Router + Audit Sink for RBAC v2
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a lightweight, pluggable authorization fabric that routes runtime and API requests to the RBAC v2 policy evaluator, emits structured audit records to the centralized audit sink, and enforces admin-level controls for Console and Dedicated flows. Objective: reduce authorization latency, standardize audit trails for compliance, and enable runtime fallbacks for scoped admin policies.
background: Current auth flow is fragmented across API gateway, console backend, and runtime shims. Each component maintains ad-hoc logging and policy checks which causes inconsistent enforcement and gaps in auditability. This ticket implements a unified fabric: a small routing layer that forwards requests to a single policy evaluator service (RBAC v2), enriches decisions with context (caller role, request route, model fingerprint, deployment tier), and writes canonical audit events to the new audit-sink topic used by observability and compliance teams.
acceptance_criteria: All API/runtime/console authorization decisions flow through the authorization fabric for supported endpoints
Median added latency for authorization <= 4ms on p95 traffic for typical request sizes
Structured audit events emitted for every decision with fields: actor_id, action, resource, decision, policy_version, request_id, route, deployment_tier
SAML SSO mapping flows through fabric and honors delegated admin groups
Fail-open/closed behavior configurable per route and tested (canary)
End-to-end tests covering policy change rollouts and canary fallbacks
Security review completed and KB entry updated
tasks: Design policy router protobuf + REST shim
Implement gRPC client to RBAC v2 evaluator with batching and trace headers
Add enrichment middleware to attach model/deployment context
Implement audit sink producer and schema (proto) for kafka/topic
Integrate SAML group mapping for delegated admin checks
Console: migrate /admin/* endpoints to call fabric
E2E tests and load tests (locust) for latency targets
Observability: dashboards and alerting for audit sink failures
design_decisions: Use a thin router written in Go to minimize cold-start and memory footprint
Synchronous policy checks via gRPC to central evaluator to ensure single source of truth
Emit audit records asynchronously to avoid amplifying request latency; guarantee at-least-once semantics
Include policy_version in audit event to support later-forensic policy regression analysis
Provide route-level configuration to choose fail-open vs fail-closed for percent-based canaries

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Central evaluator becomes QPS hotspot. Mitigation: client-side batching, local cache TTL, and autoscaling policy for evaluator pods
Risk: Audit sink outage could drop compliance logs. Mitigation: durable local staging queue with retry/backoff and alerting
Risk: SAML group sync delays leading to stale admin grants. Mitigation: short TTLs on group cache and revalidate on admin actions
